title: Infinite trees: branches, König's lemma, and Aronszajn trees

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 68–69 (§16, Lemma 16.1 and Theorem 16.3; finite repair and fresh reserves supplied explicitly)

summary: Finite levels force an infinite path; countable levels at uncountable height can prevent a cofinal path.
abstract: A tree orders nodes so that each node has a well-ordered history of predecessors. At countable height, if every level is finite, König's lemma produces one path through all levels. The analogous conclusion fails at the first uncountable height: there is a tree with countable levels but no path through every level. Its nodes can even be extended individually to every higher level, showing that such extensions need not combine into one uncountable path.
